request: Build the browser Minesweeper described in docs/SPEC.md, from scratch: the repository holds only the brief. Read the whole spec before planning. Its interfaces -- the exports of src/game/engine.ts, the page's element ids and attributes, the URL parameters and the npm scripts -- are a contract other code relies on, so follow them exactly; everything else is yours to design. Sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API and animations respect reduced motion, as the spec says. Write unit tests for the game rules and Playwright tests that drive the page. The work is done when npm run check passes, and npm run test:e2e passes against the production build, as separate gates.

Create test/engine.test.ts with Vitest covering every rule: [R8] RangeError for rows 4/51, cols 4/51, mines 0, mines rows*cols-8, non-integer rows, and valid boundary rows:5/cols:5/mines:1 not throwing; [R9] layout overriding rows/cols/mines options, adjacent set from start, 4x4 layout still RangeError; [R7] toBe identity for reveal on revealed cell, reveal on flagged cell, toggleFlag on revealed cell, chord mismatch, and any call after won/lost; [R10] first-click safety (revealed cell and all 8 neighbours not mines), pre-reveal adjacent:0/mine:false, seed determinism (same seed+cell identical layout, different cell different); [R12] flood fill stops at flagged cells and reveals bordering numbered cells only; [R13] lastRevealed exact BFS distances on an L-shaped zero region, clicked cell distance 0; [R14] loss reveals every mine and keeps flags; [R15] win on all non-mines revealed without flagging, every mine flagged; [R16] toggleFlag on revealed cell no-op, over-flagging allowed; [R17] chord reveals hidden unflagged neighbours with flood, wrong-flag chord loses, mismatched count no-op (toBe), chorded cell distance 0 not listed as newly revealed; [R18] minesLeft negative when over-flagged. Use layout boards for determinism.
